concerns: Key causal claim (senescence -> altered EV membrane integrity -> reduced intranasal recoverability) is presented as an inference in the proposal and must be tested; canonical evidence does not demonstrate this causality.

Driedonks et al. (NHP) contradicts optimistic expectations for intranasal detectability; the proposal acknowledges this but must avoid over-attributing the macaque negative result solely to source-cell senescence rather than route, labeling, formulation, or species differences (these are listed as competing explanations).

Assay- and species-sensitivity risks: MISEV2023 warns about characterization and reporting limitations—proposal must ensure orthogonal assays are validated for low-biomass, short-interval in vivo samples to avoid false negatives.

Attribution/labels: The proposal appropriately frames literature findings as background and inference rather than asserting unproven experimental facts. Ensure future reporting does not represent the proposed discriminating experiment outcomes as canonical literature evidence unless published and curated.
conclusion: The proposal is plausibly grounded in canonical evidence that (1) EV source-cell state can influence EV composition/quality and (2) orthogonal intact-EV assays and careful source control are recommended for translational rigor. MISEV2023 supports the need for orthogonal characterization and source-cell attention; rodent studies (Hermann, Kodali, Zhuang) show intranasal MSC/EV materials can reach and affect brain tissues in mice. The macaque biodistribution study (Driedonks) provides important, directly contradictory translational data for intranasal delivery in a larger species and underscores delivery/labeling/species as alternative explanations. However, there is no canonical evidence that donor-MSC senescence (p16/p21, passage) causally alters intact-EV membrane integrity or short-interval intranasal recoverability in any species. That causal link is an explicit inference and is not supported by the supplied canonical publications.
evidence_gap: No canonical evidence directly links MSC senescence markers (p16/p21 or passage number) to intact-EV membrane integrity, capture co-localization behavior, detergent/protease protection outcomes, or to altered short-interval intranasal recoverability in vivo (rodent or NHP). A program-specific experiment comparing early- versus late-passage MSC-conditioned media with the proposed orthogonal intact-EV workflow and matched short-interval intranasal dosing is required to fill this gap.
